To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best corrosion protection of electric surfaces is achieved by using noble metals such as gold or silver.

the corrosion protection of electric contacts is very challenging and that the best way to achieve a long service life of electrical contacts is to use a combination of different means to prevent corrosion.
the corrosion resistance of electrical contacts can be significantly improved by the use of noble plating materials and the application of protective coatings.

the use of noble plating materials is not always a guarantee for a long service life of electrically conductable surfaces.

the corrosion behavior and the contact resistance of electrical contacts can be improved by the use of different coating materials, by the use of special coating processes and by the use of suitable surface pretreatment.
the corrosion resistance of electric surfaces is a very complex and multifaceted topic, for which there are no simple solutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the corrosion resistance of electric contact materials is very complex and that the development of new corrosion protection methods for electric contacts is still a challenging task.

the use of gold as a plating material for corrosion protection of electrical contacts is still a good choice, but the use of palladium as an undercoat for gold plating is a good way to reduce the consumption of gold and to increase corrosion resistance of gold.

gold is a very suitable material to protect electrically conductive contacts from corrosion.
there is a need to use more noble plating materials and to develop new corrosion resistant plating materials.
the use of palladium and palladium alloy plating can significantly improve the corrosion resistance of electric conductive surfaces.
